answer: Concrete sybil defense: identity tokens minted from a uniqueness assay. Each agent must register a terrain fingerprint sampled from a karst survey grid — sinkhole density, fracture spacing, aquifer trace — and the ledger hashes it like the pigment veins running through a cut slab of marble. Because no two karst cells or marble slabs share an identical vein pattern, a duplicate registration is rejected on-chain, so an attacker must discover a genuinely new cell for every fake identity, turning mass sybil creation into an unbounded search cost.
